problem.statement: Find theta=Arg(z) for z=i*(-1)=-i, using the principal-argument convention -pi<theta<=pi. Step 2 forms an unwrapped argument candidate only; every asserted equality remains a claim of the displayed derivation.
problem.goal: Judge the derivation and the claimed principal value, distinguishing an unwrapped argument from a principal argument.

conditions.description: The principal argument lies in (-pi,pi]; pi is included and -pi is excluded.
The fixed complex input is z=i*(-1)=-i, which is nonzero.

assumptions.description: An argument candidate is retained only when it belongs to the stated principal interval.
The complex input whose argument is requested is nonzero.
The imaginary unit satisfies i squared = -1.

methods.name: Displayed derivation
methods.description: Compute the factor arguments, form an unwrapped argument candidate, and select a principal value.

steps.explanation: Evaluate the two factor principal arguments.
Form an unwrapped argument candidate; this step does not claim that theta_0 is principal.
Accept the candidate as the principal argument.

annotations.basis: The stipulated interval gives Arg(i)=pi/2 and Arg(-1)=pi.
The sum 3*pi/2 is an argument of -i because exp(3*pi*i/2)=-i. Only an unwrapped candidate is claimed.
The candidate 3*pi/2 exceeds pi and is excluded by the stated principal domain. The first invalid acceptance is Step 3.

mathematical_basis: A nonzero complex number has arguments differing by integer multiples of 2*pi; the principal argument selects the unique representative in (-pi,pi].
The unwrapped candidate theta_0=3*pi/2 has the correct complex unit direction, so Step 2 is not an arithmetic or branch-equality error.

Step 3 accepts a candidate of the angle equation exp(i*theta)=-i outside its required interval. This is the existing extraneous_root reason: a candidate was accepted as an original solution without the domain check.
Subtracting 2*pi gives -pi/2 in the required interval, so the claimed principal value is incorrect. The other premises already hold and do not repair branch selection.
rubric.remediation: Normalize the unwrapped argument by subtracting 2*pi and verify the result belongs to (-pi,pi] before calling it Arg.
